findings.title: The shared-response schema strips expiry and refresh-token fields
findings.body: Using a Zod schema's toString() as a computed property name does not create a wildcard validator. These properties become literal keys (normally "[object Object]"), and z.object strips unrecognized fields. With credential sharing enabled, a response containing access_token, expires_in and refresh_token therefore loses its expiry and refresh token. Zoom subsequently calculates an invalid expiry, and Office 365 cannot retain the returned expiry. Define explicit response fields or use an appropriate catchall/passthrough schema.

findings.title: Google refresh persists the safeParse result instead of credential data
findings.body: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the safeParse wrapper { success: true, data: ... }, unlike the previous googleCredentialSchema.parse call, which returned the credentials themselves. Saving this wrapper as Credential.key removes access_token and the other expected fields from the top level. After any successful refresh, including with syncing disabled, the next GoogleCalendarService construction fails googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key). Persist the parsed data rather than the wrapper.

findings.title: The sync branch returns a different response type from SDK refreshes
findings.body: The sync branch returns an unparsed fetch Response, but several callers expect their refresh callback's SDK-specific return value. Google reads res.data, Zoho CRM and Bigin read tokenInfo.data, and HubSpot reads accessToken/expiresIn directly. A fetch Response has none of those fields, so enabling syncing causes these integrations to throw or use undefined tokens even when the endpoint returns valid JSON. Normalize and decode the sync response into the contract expected by each caller.

findings.title: Do not replace an omitted refresh token with a dummy token
findings.body: The helper inserts the literal "refresh_token" whenever the response omits refresh_token, even when credential sharing is disabled. Office365CalendarService accepts refresh responses without a new refresh token and merges parsed fields into its existing credentials; this new dummy field overwrites the valid stored refresh token. The next refresh then sends the dummy value to Microsoft and fails. Preserve the existing refresh token when the provider does not return a replacement.

findings.title: Import Prisma before using the new credential update
findings.body: The new refresh path calls prisma.credential.update, but this file has no prisma import or declaration. This fails TypeScript checking and, if executed without checking, throws ReferenceError after Salesforce successfully returns a token. Import the Prisma client used by the other integration services.

findings.title: Salesforce refresh bypasses the configured credential-sync endpoint
findings.body: The new Salesforce refresh unconditionally posts to Salesforce rather than using refreshOAuthTokens. Thus, even with credential sharing and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT configured, Cal.com independently refreshes the provider token and requires a locally stored refresh token. An external app store supplying only an access token cannot keep this integration working, and it is not the source of truth for refreshes as it is for the other integrations. Route this refresh through the sync helper.

findings.title: Pass the Bigin credential owner's user ID, not its credential ID
findings.body: refreshOAuthTokens treats its third argument as a user ID and sends it as calcomUserId, but Bigin passes credentialId. Credential IDs and user IDs are unrelated, so a sync endpoint will either fail to locate the account or return another user's token when the numbers happen to match. Carry credential.userId through to this call while retaining credentialId only for the database update.

findings.title: Use the installed Zoom app slug in sync requests
findings.body: The refresh request sends appSlug="zoomvideo", while the Zoom OAuth callback creates credentials with appId="zoom" and the new webhook resolves applications by their actual slug. A parent app store using that same slug to look up credentials cannot resolve this refresh request. Send "zoom" consistently with the credential and webhook contracts.

findings.title: The advertised minimal sync response is incompatible with provider parsers
findings.body: The helper says the sync endpoint should return only an access token and expiry, but its fetch-based callers still require provider-specific response structures. Webex validates scope, token_type, refresh_token and refresh_token_expires_in; Lark requires a success code and nested data containing refresh-token expiry fields. An endpoint implementing the stated minimal contract cannot refresh either integration. Add adapters that merge the minimal response with existing credentials, or define and document the provider-specific contract actually required.
